narrativeReportMd:
# ExplanationOfBenefit R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Hard local breaking changes were found. The most important R4-to-R6 instance breaks are the required `patient` element being replaced by required `subject`, dental/body-site data changing from CodeableConcept fields into repeating backbone structures, and several scalar or local elements being removed or reshaped. R6 also relaxes multiple formerly required billing fields and widens many choice/reference domains, which is not an R4-to-R6 validation break but is a significant R6-to-R4 and runtime-contract risk.

## Scope
The analysis used the packaged R4 4.0.1 and R6 6.0.0-ballot4 StructureDefinitions for the base resource and checked selected related ValueSets and CodeSystems. Inherited base-artifact changes were excluded according to the assignment rule.

## Main migration themes
Migration is not just additive. Some R4 JSON properties must be renamed or transformed (`patient` to `subject`, `diagnosis.packageCode` to root `diagnosisRelatedGroup`), some must be structurally reshaped (`item.bodySite`, `addItem.bodySite`, `processNote.type`), and some R6-valid data cannot be represented in R4 without extensions or loss (`Group` subjects, newly optional formerly required fields, broader supportingInfo.value[x], and added request/reference targets).

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `ExplanationOfBenefit:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:patient-subject:9f0b35`, `ExplanationOfBenefit:SERIALIZATION_OR_CODEGEN:bodySite:4c2d18`, `ExplanationOfBenefit:SERIALIZATION_OR_CODEGEN:processNote-type:5b7f8a`, and `ExplanationOfBenefit:CARDINALITY:required-relaxed:21ad90`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for business-semantics mappings where the StructureDefinition shows the shape change but not the intended migration policy: care-team responsibility and specialty, diagnosis related group relocation, adjudication non-monetary value conversion, and process-note language terminology enforcement.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes could have been less disruptive if old elements were retained as deprecated aliases, if new semantics were introduced as optional additions first, or if stricter requirements were placed in profiles rather than the base resource. The tradeoff would have been more parallel ways to express the same adjudication data.

## Follow-up analysis
Terminology expansion, official cross-version maps, and IG-specific profiles should be checked before implementing a production migration pipeline.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: ExplanationOfBenefit has multiple local hard breaking changes between R4 and R6. The top migration concerns are required `patient` becoming required `subject`, body-site and process-note serialization shape changes, and R6 data that cannot be round-tripped to R4 because requiredness was relaxed and choice/reference domains were widened. Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition differences, with moderate uncertainty about official migration intent and terminology expansion details.
summary.migrationThemesMd: The main themes are element identity changes, representation changes, and model widening. R4 data generally needs active transforms rather than field-for-field copying. R6-to-R4 conversion is harder for new or wider content: Group subjects, added request targets, broader supportingInfo.value[x] types, omitted insurer/provider/insurance/productOrService, and added financial/review fields require policy decisions or extensions.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local snapshot deltas because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is lower for business justification, prevalence, and exact terminology validation because no official diff, ConceptMap, narrative ballot rationale, terminology-server expansion, or real-world corpus was available.

findings.title: Required patient was replaced by required subject with an expanded Patient-or-Group target

semanticText.short: The recipient of the products and services
semanticText.definition: The party to whom the professional services and/or products have been supplied or are being considered and for whom actual for forecast reimbursement is sought.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 instances identify the covered recipient with the mandatory `patient` property.

newState.summary: R6 removes patient and adds required subject 1..1 as Reference(Patient|Group).

semanticText.short: The recipient(s) of the products and services
semanticText.definition: The party/group to whom the professional services and/or products have been supplied or are being considered and for whom actual for forecast reimbursement is sought.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses `subject` for the same role and broadens the domain to groups as well as individual patients.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element is mandatory in both releases, has nearly identical requirements text, and the R6 definition explicitly generalizes the R4 patient party to a party/group subject.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A valid R4 instance containing `patient` but no `subject` will fail R6 validation because `patient` is no longer a known local element and `subject` is required. Generated models and queries that dereference `patient` also break. In the reverse direction, an R6 `subject` that references a Group cannot be represented by R4 `patient` without changing meaning or using an extension.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Mis-mapping the claim recipient can affect adjudication history, coverage coordination, and patient/group-level financial interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize the beneficiary of services from only Patient to a subject that can also be a Group.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain required `patient` but widen it to Reference(Patient|Group) with clearer subject/recipient definitions.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Generalizing the service recipient from only Patient to Patient or Group is a reasonable R6 goal, but the hard required-property rename was not necessary to meet that core goal. Keeping the old path and broadening its target would preserve R4-valid instances while still allowing Group recipients, with only a naming-consistency tradeoff.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `ExplanationOfBenefit.patient` as `1..1 Reference(Patient|Group)` and updated the short/definition to say recipient or subject. The name would be awkward for Group references, but living with a legacy name is a legitimate compatibility option. Adding `subject` while also retaining `patient` would create duplicate same-fact fields, so the cleaner backward-compatible alternative is to broaden the existing path rather than remove it.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances and avoids duplicate fields, at the cost of carrying a nonoptimal `patient` name for Group beneficiaries.

evidence.detail: R4 defines patient as min=1 max=1 Reference(Patient).
R6 defines subject as min=1 max=1 Reference(Patient|Group).
No local R6 patient element exists.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments show only the affected property, not complete valid resources.

findings.narrativeMd: `ExplanationOfBenefit.patient` is a required R4 element but is absent in R6; R6 instead requires `ExplanationOfBenefit.subject`. This is a direct field identity and JSON property break for validators, serializers, generated classes, FHIRPath, search extraction code, and application logic that assumes a Patient-only beneficiary.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance with `patient` but no `subject` cannot validate against R6. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: `subject` can reference Group, which R4 `patient` cannot carry. Patient-to-Patient mappings are straightforward, but Group subjects require a policy decision.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `patient` to `subject` for Patient references during R4-to-R6 migration. Update generated model accessors, FHIRPath expressions, search mappings, and authorization/business rules. For R6-to-R4, reject, extension-map, or split Group-subject records according to local policy; do not silently coerce a Group to a Patient.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The broader subject model is understandable, but making the old required property disappear creates a hard break. A deprecated `patient` alias or cross-version extension would have reduced disruption while preserving the new generalized `subject` semantics.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `patient` was a required R4 element and `subject` is the required R6 replacement, so ordinary R4 EOB instances and generated accessors break unless a transform runs. The Group target addition is understandable, but the same core recipient role could have been introduced with a less disruptive base design. Because this is the central beneficiary/recipient path for a financial resource, the rename deserves renewed review.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `ExplanationOfBenefit.patient` is 1..1 `Reference(Patient)`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `ExplanationOfBenefit.subject` is 1..1 `Reference(Patient|Group)`.
R6 StructureDefinition checked: no local `ExplanationOfBenefit.patient` element is present.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral: it does not impose normative immutability, but it also does not soften a required, central billing-recipient path enough to ignore an avoidable wire rename.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 JSON with required `patient` lacks required R6 `subject`; generated APIs, FHIRPath, authorization, and mapping code also need path changes, and Group subjects create R6-to-R4 loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could have retained `patient` with an expanded target or retained it as a deprecated alias while adding `subject`. The tradeoff is an awkward legacy name for Group recipients or duplicate recipient fields, but the field is central enough that a transition design looks plausible.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the prior report correctly identified a high-confidence hard break and a plausible less-breaking design; the fresh review likewise treats it as worth revisiting.

findings.title: item and addItem bodySite changed from a CodeableConcept plus subSite fields to repeating backbone structures

oldState.summary: R4 represented bodySite as optional CodeableConcept 0..1 and subSite as sibling CodeableConcept 0..* on item and addItem.

binding.description: The code for the teeth, quadrant, sextant and arch.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 JSON uses a single object property such as `item[0].bodySite` and a separate repeating `item[0].subSite` array.

newState.summary: R6 represents bodySite as repeating BackboneElement 0..* with required site 1..* CodeableReference(BodyStructure) and nested subSite 0..* CodeableConcept.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 JSON uses an array of body-site components, each containing `site` and optionally `subSite`; the site coding can also be a CodeableReference to BodyStructure.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same tooth and surface bindings move from the old fields to the nested R6 `site` and `subSite` children.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON shape changes. R4 `bodySite` is a CodeableConcept object on a non-repeating element; R6 `bodySite` is a repeating backbone array with mandatory `site`. R4 sibling `subSite` is unknown in R6. Conversely, R6 can carry multiple body-site groups and BodyStructure references that R4 cannot faithfully flatten.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dental and anatomical adjudication can depend on precise site/surface mapping; flattening errors can affect payment rules.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow multiple body-site groups and link coded sites with specific sub-sites and BodyStructure references.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep old `bodySite` and `subSite` as deprecated shorthand while adding a distinct detailed body-site backbone.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable: the new backbone can group multiple sites with their sub-sites and can reference BodyStructure, which the R4 flat fields cannot express cleanly. A compatibility design exists, but it would leave two same-resource ways to represent body-site facts and would not make old flat `subSite` data unambiguous.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained the R4 `bodySite` CodeableConcept and sibling `subSite` fields, marked them deprecated, and added a new detailed backbone under a different name. That would preserve old payloads for common single-site cases. The material tradeoff is indefinite support for parallel simple and detailed representations, including validation ambiguity when both are populated or when old `subSite` values cannot be confidently attached to one of several sites.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves simple R4 dental/body-site instances, but duplicates anatomical-location representations and requires precedence and consistency rules.

evidence.detail: R4 item.bodySite is 0..1 CodeableConcept bound to ValueSet/tooth.
R4 item.subSite is 0..* CodeableConcept bound to ValueSet/surface.
R6 item.bodySite is 0..* BackboneElement.
R6 bodySite.site is 1..* CodeableReference with target BodyStructure and the tooth binding.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows the intended nesting pattern; exact CodeableReference JSON shape may vary by implementation library.

findings.narrativeMd: The body-site model was locally restructured for both adjudicated `item` lines and insurer-added `addItem` lines. This breaks old parsers and serializers because the property name `bodySite` remains but no longer has the same cardinality or datatype, and `subSite` moved under each bodySite component.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with `bodySite` as a CodeableConcept object or sibling `subSite` elements will not satisfy the R6 element type and path rules. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: multiple bodySite repetitions, multiple required sites per component, or BodyStructure references cannot be losslessly mapped into R4 0..1 bodySite plus flat subSite.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Transform each R4 `bodySite` and associated `subSite` values into one R6 bodySite component. When R4 has subSite without bodySite, create a policy for deriving a site or carrying the data in an extension, because R6 bodySite components require at least one site. Test dental/oral claims with multiple surfaces and missing sites.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The grouped structure better models site-to-subsite relationships, but removing the old scalar structure is disruptive. Retaining deprecated simple fields or providing a formal ConceptMap/StructureMap would have reduced migration ambiguity.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `item.bodySite` and `addItem.bodySite` changed from a simple coded property with sibling `subSite` arrays into repeating backbone components with required `site` and nested `subSite`. That is a real JSON and SDK break for dental/anatomic adjudication data, but the R6 structure has a clear modeling benefit: it can group sites with their sub-sites and use BodyStructure references. Preserving the old shape would leave two competing anatomical-location representations.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: item/addItem `bodySite` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept`; sibling `subSite` is 0..* `CodeableConcept`.
R6 StructureDefinition: item/addItem `bodySite` is 0..* `BackboneElement`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `bodySite.site` is 1..* `CodeableReference(BodyStructure)` and `bodySite.subSite` is nested 0..* `CodeableConcept`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; the judgment turns on the concrete serialization break and the reasonableness of the richer location model.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `bodySite` objects and sibling `subSite` arrays do not match the R6 array/backbone shape; R6 multiple sites or BodyStructure references are not losslessly representable in R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have kept deprecated simple `bodySite`/`subSite` fields and added a distinct detailed backbone. That would preserve many R4 instances but creates duplicate location channels and hard consistency rules, especially when old flat sub-sites must be related to one of several sites.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the prior report correctly found a high-confidence hard serialization break and only a partial alternative; its High impact feels somewhat strong for an optional, mostly model-improving path.

findings.title: processNote.type changed from required-bound code to CodeableConcept and processNote.text changed from string to markdown

oldState.summary: R4 processNote.type was code 0..1 with required note-type binding; processNote.text was string.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Packaged CodeSystem note-type contains display, print, and printoper in both releases.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 note type is serialized as a primitive string property such as `type: "display"`.

newState.summary: R6 processNote.type is CodeableConcept 0..1 with extensible note-type binding; processNote.text is markdown.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 note type is a CodeableConcept object; note text remains a JSON primitive but generated type systems may distinguish markdown from string.

facts.note: CodeSystem codes checked in package files.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The note type JSON representation changes from a primitive code to a CodeableConcept object. Existing R4 instances and generated classes that treat the value as a string will fail R6 shape validation. R6 CodeableConcepts with multiple codings, text-only concepts, or out-of-set extensible codings do not map cleanly to a single R4 required code.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Process notes may carry adjudication explanations and print/display instructions; losing note type can alter remittance presentation.

justification.inferredGoal: Make note purpose terminology extensible and richer than a required primitive code.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain primitive `processNote.type` and add an optional CodeableConcept sibling for richer note-purpose coding.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing CodeableConcept note purposes is a coherent goal because it supports local systems, display text, and multiple codings. The old primitive code could be preserved only by adding a parallel concept field; that compatibility path would materially complicate the model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base R6 design could have kept `processNote.type` as the R4 primitive code and introduced a new optional CodeableConcept element such as `typeConcept`. A choice redesign would not preserve old JSON because it would introduce suffixed properties. The sibling approach preserves old instances, but risks indefinite use of the deprecated primitive and disagreement between primitive and CodeableConcept representations. The `text` string-to-markdown change is a generated-type concern, but the main old-valid/new-invalid issue is the `type` shape.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids the primitive-to-object wire break, but creates duplicate note-purpose fields and conflict rules for primitive versus concept values.

evidence.detail: R4 type is code with required note-type binding.
R6 type is CodeableConcept with extensible note-type binding.
R4 text is string.
R6 text is markdown.

examples.examplesMd: The text value remains a JSON string, but systems that distinguish primitive FHIR types should treat it as markdown in R6.

findings.narrativeMd: `processNote.type` is no longer a primitive code. This affects wire-format validation, generated classes, enum switches, and display logic. The `processNote.text` string-to-markdown change is less likely to invalidate JSON, but it changes generated type names and may affect rendering and sanitization expectations.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: a primitive `processNote.type` string is not a CodeableConcept in R6. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: a CodeableConcept with multiple codings or only free text cannot be collapsed to R4 required code without choosing one coding or losing information.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap R4 note type codes in a CodeableConcept using the note-type CodeSystem. Review markdown rendering/sanitization paths for note text. For R6-to-R4, define precedence rules for choosing a single code and reject or extension-map text-only concepts.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer CodeableConcept model is defensible, but changing an existing primitive property is a classic serialization break. A choice or additional element would have been easier for cross-version clients.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `processNote.type` changed from a primitive required-bound code to an optional CodeableConcept, while `processNote.text` changed from string to markdown. Existing note-type strings must be wrapped for R6, so serializers and generated models break. The R6 goal of richer/extensible note-purpose coding is credible, and keeping both primitive and CodeableConcept note-purpose fields would create duplicate semantics.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `processNote.type` is 0..1 `code` with required `note-type|4.0.1` binding.
R6 StructureDefinition: `processNote.type` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept` with extensible `note-type` binding.
R4/R6 local CodeSystem `note-type` concepts checked: display, print, and printoper are retained.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; this optional process-note path has real migration work, but the maturity context does not make the richer datatype disproportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a primitive `processNote.type` string is not the R6 CodeableConcept shape; generated enum/string accessors change, and richer R6 CodeableConcepts may not reduce to one R4 code.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have kept the primitive `type` and added a sibling concept element, but that would require precedence and conflict rules for two note-purpose representations. A choice redesign would not preserve the old `type` wire name.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the prior report correctly identifies the hard shape break and partial alternative; I would not weight the optional note path as strongly as the prior High overall impact.

findings.title: supportingInfo.timing[x] replaced date with dateTime and added Timing

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 choice suffix for a single date is `timingDate`.

newState.summary: R6 allows timingDateTime, timingPeriod, or timingTiming.
newState.narrativeMd: The single-date flavor is now represented by the dateTime type and therefore uses the `timingDateTime` JSON choice suffix.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Although many FHIR date lexical values can be carried by dateTime, the JSON choice property name changes. An R4 instance using `timingDate` will not match the R6 choice element. R6 instances using `Timing` or time precision beyond a simple date may not be representable in R4.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow more precise dates/times and recurring Timing for supporting information.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `timingDate` as an allowed choice while adding `timingDateTime` and `timingTiming`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding dateTime precision and Timing recurrence is reasonable, but removing the old `date` choice is not needed to achieve that expressiveness. A date is a narrower temporal representation that can coexist with dateTime and Timing in the same choice set.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have allowed `date`, `dateTime`, `Period`, and `Timing` on `supportingInfo.timing[x]`. That preserves R4 `timingDate` payloads and adds the new R6 capabilities. The tradeoff is a slightly broader temporal choice set and continued presence of a less precise date option, but it is low to moderate because only one timing choice can be present.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds overlapping date/dateTime choices, but the existing max 1 choice cardinality limits ambiguity and preserves old instances.

evidence.detail: R4 types are date and Period.
R6 types are dateTime, Period, and Timing.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments are illustrative and omit unrelated required resource content.

findings.narrativeMd: `supportingInfo.timing[x]` keeps the same conceptual role but changes one choice type and adds another. Choice-type changes are wire-format changes because the type code is part of the JSON property name.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: `timingDate` is an R4 choice property that is not allowed by the R6 choice list. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: `timingTiming` and high-precision `timingDateTime` values require either simplification to a date/Period or an extension in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `timingDate` to `timingDateTime` when the value is a single date and preserve the lexical date if that is clinically sufficient. Define downgrade rules for R6 Timing values before any R6-to-R4 conversion.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This likely supports better temporal precision, but retaining `date` as a choice would have avoided invalidating the old property suffix. The compatibility cost of retaining it seems modest compared with the migration burden.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `supportingInfo.timing[x]` replaced the R4 `date` choice with `dateTime` and added `Timing`. A date value can be carried at date precision in dateTime, but the JSON choice suffix changes from `timingDate` to `timingDateTime`, making old instances fail strict R6 parsing. The R6 expressiveness goal could likely have been met by adding dateTime and Timing while keeping date.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `supportingInfo.timing[x]` allows `date` or `Period`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `supportingInfo.timing[x]` allows `dateTime`, `Period`, or `Timing`.
FHIR JSON choice names are type-derived, so R4 `timingDate` and R6 `timingDateTime` are different properties.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; absent normative pressure, the low-cost compatibility option of retaining `date` is decisive.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `timingDate` is not an R6 choice property; R6 `timingTiming` or high-precision dateTime values create reverse-conversion policy issues.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could allow `date`, `dateTime`, `Period`, and `Timing` on the same choice. That preserves old `timingDate` payloads and still adds precision/recurrence; the main tradeoff is overlapping date/dateTime choices, limited by max 1 choice cardinality.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the prior report correctly found an avoidable choice-suffix break with a straightforward less-breaking base design.

findings.title: careTeam.responsible and careTeam.qualification were removed; specialty was added as a partial replacement

oldState.summary: R4 careTeam had optional responsible 0..1 boolean and qualification 0..1 CodeableConcept.

semanticText.short: Indicator of the lead practitioner / Practitioner credential or specialization

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could mark the lead or responsible party directly and carry provider qualification/specialization under `qualification`.

newState.summary: R6 has no responsible or qualification element; it adds optional specialty 0..1 CodeableConcept using the same provider-qualification value set.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps a specialization-like concept under `specialty` but does not preserve the R4 responsibility boolean.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `qualification` and `specialty` share the binding and similar requirements, but the wording narrows from qualification/credential to specialization. `responsible` has no obvious direct replacement.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances containing `careTeam.responsible` or `careTeam.qualification` will contain unknown elements in R6. Generated models and business rules that identify the lead provider or provider credentials from those elements need redesign. R6 `specialty` can often be mapped to R4 `qualification`, but the semantic equivalence is not exact.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Lead provider and qualification/specialty data can affect routing, billing responsibility, and audit interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify care-team details and distinguish specialty from credential/qualification.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain optional `responsible` and `qualification` with clarified or deprecated definitions, adding `specialty` only if distinct semantics are needed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is not clearly evidenced beyond simplifying or renaming care-team details. Because both R4 fields were optional, retaining them would preserve valid R4 instances with modest base-model burden, especially for `responsible`, which has no direct R6 replacement.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 design could have kept `careTeam.responsible` and `careTeam.qualification` at `0..1`, clarified that `qualification` may represent the applicable specialization, and optionally added `specialty` only if it is intended to be distinct. If both `qualification` and `specialty` were retained, guidance would be needed to avoid duplicate or conflicting specialization facts, but the old `responsible` flag is a separate concept and could have been preserved without that duplication.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Carries legacy care-team fields and may need qualification/specialty guidance, but it preserves lead-provider data and does not block R6 use.

evidence.detail: R4 defines responsible as 0..1 boolean.
R4 defines qualification as 0..1 CodeableConcept bound to provider-qualification.
R6 defines specialty as 0..1 CodeableConcept bound to provider-qualification.

examples.examplesMd: The extension URL is illustrative; production migrations should use a governed extension or IG rule.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 removes two care-team fields with practical billing semantics. `qualification` has an apparent partial successor in `specialty`, but `responsible` does not. This is both a validation break and a potential business-rule break for systems that determine lead provider responsibility from the EOB.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: R4 care-team entries with `responsible` or `qualification` no longer match R6 paths. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: `specialty` can be back-mapped only if the implementation accepts specialty as a qualification, and there is no R6 base field to reconstruct `responsible`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `qualification` to `specialty` only after confirming local code semantics. Preserve `responsible` with a cross-version extension, claim-level provider role, or IG-specific rule if the lead-provider flag matters. Add regression tests for multi-provider claims.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The specialty rename may improve terminology, but dropping the old paths without aliases is avoidable from a compatibility perspective. The best backward-compatible option would have retained deprecated fields and documented precedence rules.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed to decide whether each R4 qualification code is truly a specialty and how to preserve lead-provider responsibility.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 removes `careTeam.responsible` and `careTeam.qualification`; `specialty` only partially replaces qualification and does not replace the lead/responsible flag. This can invalidate old care-team entries and lose billing-responsibility meaning for multi-provider claims. Because both old fields were optional and one has no R6 base replacement, retaining them as deprecated or clarified fields appears practical.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `careTeam.responsible` is 0..1 boolean for the lead/responsible practitioner.
R4 StructureDefinition: `careTeam.qualification` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept` bound to provider-qualification.
R6 StructureDefinition: `careTeam.specialty` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept` with the provider-qualification binding; no `responsible` or `qualification` elements are present.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral, but billing responsibility and provider qualification are business-relevant enough that maturity does not make removal harmless.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 care-team entries containing `responsible` or `qualification` use paths absent from R6; preserving `responsible` requires an extension or other policy.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could retain optional `responsible` and `qualification`, deprecating or clarifying them while adding `specialty` if distinct. The main tradeoff is guidance needed to prevent duplicate qualification/specialty facts; `responsible` is a separate boolean and has little conflict risk.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the prior report's medium impact and less-breaking alternative are supported; I give it a Revisit action judgment because one removed field has no base replacement.

findings.title: diagnosis.packageCode moved from each diagnosis to root diagnosisRelatedGroup

oldState.summary: R4 carried package billing or DRG code as optional diagnosis.packageCode under each diagnosis repetition.

binding.description: The DRG codes associated with the diagnosis.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 model allowed the package code to be associated with a specific diagnosis entry.

newState.summary: R6 removes diagnosis.packageCode and adds root-level diagnosisRelatedGroup 0..1 CodeableConcept with the same example binding.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 model carries only one package/DRG code for the EOB as a whole.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The short, definition, comments, and binding are materially the same, but the parent changed from diagnosis to resource root.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with `diagnosis.packageCode` use a removed path. Moving the code to root also changes cardinality relative to the resource: multiple diagnoses could each carry a packageCode in R4, while R6 has one root-level diagnosisRelatedGroup. A single-code mapping is straightforward; multiple distinct codes require business policy.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: DRG/package grouping can drive reimbursement; collapsing multiple diagnosis-associated codes can alter adjudication interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent diagnosis related group as a claim/EOB-level grouping rather than as an attribute of individual diagnoses.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated `diagnosis.packageCode` while adding root `diagnosisRelatedGroup` with consistency guidance.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving a DRG/package code to resource level is conceptually plausible because DRG is often claim-level. The less-breaking path is only partial because the R4 location allowed one package code per diagnosis, while the R6 location intentionally permits one code for the whole EOB.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `diagnosis.packageCode` as deprecated and added `diagnosisRelatedGroup`, with an invariant or guidance that old nested values should agree with the root value. That would preserve old instances when there is a single package code. It would also keep two locations for the same reimbursement grouping and would not cleanly resolve R4 instances with multiple distinct per-diagnosis package codes.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common single-DRG R4 cases, but duplicates the DRG location and leaves ambiguous multiple per-diagnosis package codes.

evidence.detail: R4 defines diagnosis.packageCode as 0..1 CodeableConcept under diagnosis.
R6 defines diagnosisRelatedGroup as 0..1 CodeableConcept at the resource root.

examples.examplesMd: If more than one R4 diagnosis has a different packageCode, the migration is not automatically lossless.

findings.narrativeMd: `diagnosis.packageCode` was removed and its apparent successor is root `diagnosisRelatedGroup`. The value set and wording make the match strong, but the move changes the data model from per-diagnosis to per-resource.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: the nested R4 path is absent in R6. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: a root diagnosisRelatedGroup can be copied to one or more R4 diagnosis entries only by policy; if no diagnosis exists, R4 has no natural local slot.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, move a single packageCode to `diagnosisRelatedGroup`. If multiple distinct packageCode values occur, flag the record for adjudication-domain review or preserve extras in extensions. Update analytics that join DRG to diagnosis sequence.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The root location may be semantically cleaner, but the migration would be safer with a formal map and a deprecation period for the nested element.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed for records with multiple diagnosis repetitions carrying packageCode.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `diagnosis.packageCode` moved from each diagnosis repetition to a single root `diagnosisRelatedGroup`. The value set and wording make the intended successor clear, but the parent and effective cardinality changed: R4 could carry different package/DRG codes per diagnosis, while R6 has only one for the resource. That collapse can be financially meaningful and may require adjudication-domain judgment.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `diagnosis.packageCode` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept` under each diagnosis, bound to `ex-diagnosisrelatedgroup`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `diagnosisRelatedGroup` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept` at the resource root with the same binding.
Definitions/comments checked: both describe package billing or DRG-style grouping for a health condition.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; the concern comes from reimbursement semantics and a possible cardinality collapse, not from high maturity pressure.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the nested R4 path is absent in R6; multiple distinct R4 nested codes cannot be automatically represented by one R6 root value.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial but strong enough to reconsider. R6 could keep deprecated `diagnosis.packageCode` while adding the root field and guidance that single nested values migrate to the root. This duplicates the DRG location and leaves multi-code cases ambiguous, but it would preserve common old instances and expose conflicts rather than silently collapsing them.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the prior report correctly found a hard move and only a partial alternative; I place more action weight on the lossy per-diagnosis-to-root cardinality change.

findings.title: item.adjudication.value decimal was removed and replaced by adjudication.quantity Quantity

oldState.summary: R4 item.adjudication.value was optional decimal for non-monetary adjudication values.

semanticText.definition: A non-monetary value associated with the category. Mutually exclusive to the amount element above.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented percentages or fixed non-money values as a bare decimal.

newState.summary: R6 removes value and adds item.adjudication.quantity 0..1 Quantity for the same non-monetary role.

semanticText.definition: A non-monetary value associated with the category. Mutually exclusive to the amount element above.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses Quantity, allowing a value with unit/system/code metadata.

facts.oldValue: Non-monetary value associated with the category.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 value and R6 quantity elements share the same short, definition, comment, and requirements text, with decimal replaced by Quantity.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The R4 `value` property is absent in R6, and the replacement has a different datatype. Existing decimal JSON cannot be copied in place. R6 Quantity values with units are richer than an R4 decimal and may lose unit semantics on downgrade.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Adjudication percentages, counts, or rate-like quantities can affect payment calculations; unit assumptions need review.

justification.inferredGoal: Give non-monetary adjudication values explicit Quantity semantics rather than unlabelled decimals.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain decimal `adjudication.value` as a deprecated unitless shorthand while adding `adjudication.quantity`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using Quantity for non-monetary adjudication values is reasonable because percentages, counts, days, and other values can need unit metadata. A compatibility design exists, but it would leave a deprecated unitless decimal alongside the richer Quantity representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept `item.adjudication.value` as the R4 decimal and added `item.adjudication.quantity` for unit-bearing values. That preserves R4 instances and supports the new goal for richer data. The tradeoff is material because both fields would represent the same adjudication fact, requiring mutual-exclusion or precedence rules and risking indefinite use of an ambiguous unitless decimal.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old decimals but creates duplicate non-monetary value fields and conflict rules; the old decimal still cannot carry units.

evidence.detail: R4 defines value as 0..1 decimal and R6 has no such element.
R6 defines quantity as 0..1 Quantity with the same non-monetary adjudication definition.

examples.examplesMd: A unitless Quantity preserves the R4 decimal but may not be semantically sufficient for all categories.

findings.narrativeMd: `item.adjudication.value` is removed and the non-monetary adjudication concept now appears as `quantity`. This is a validation and code-generation break for item-level adjudication data.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 adjudication with `value` is invalid in R6. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: a Quantity with unit, comparator, or system/code metadata cannot be represented as a bare decimal without loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map decimal `value` to `quantity.value`; infer or add units only when category-specific rules make that safe. For R6-to-R4, define category-specific downgrade rules and preserve unit metadata in extensions if needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The stronger Quantity datatype is clinically and financially clearer, but the same goal could have been achieved with a new optional element and a deprecation period for `value`.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `item.adjudication.value` was a unitless decimal and R6 replaces it with `item.adjudication.quantity`. R4 decimals must be transformed, and R6 Quantity units can be lossy when downgrading. Still, the R6 goal is strong: non-monetary adjudication values such as percentages, counts, or days often need unit metadata, and retaining both value and quantity would duplicate the same adjudication fact.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `item.adjudication.value` is 0..1 `decimal` for a non-monetary value.
R6 StructureDefinition: `item.adjudication.quantity` is 0..1 `Quantity` with the same short/definition/comment.
R6 StructureDefinition checked: no local `item.adjudication.value` element is present.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; financial calculation relevance requires care, but it does not outweigh the clearer Quantity datatype.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 decimal `value` property is not accepted on the R6 adjudication component; R6 Quantity unit/system/comparator metadata cannot be represented by a bare R4 decimal.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could retain deprecated decimal `value` and add `quantity`, but then validators and implementers need mutual-exclusion or precedence rules for two non-monetary adjudication value fields. The old decimal also remains semantically ambiguous.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the prior medium-impact, partial-alternative assessment matches the fresh review; the break is real but proportionate.

findings.title: Several R4 required billing fields became optional in R6

affectedLocation.oldPath: ExplanationOfBenefit.insurance / insurer / provider / item.productOrService and nested productOrService elements

oldState.summary: R4 required insurance 1..*, insurer 1..1, provider 1..1, and productOrService 1..1 on item/detail/subDetail/addItem/detail/subDetail.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 base validation guaranteed at least one insurance, an insurer, a provider, and service/product codes on line structures.

newState.summary: R6 relaxes those minimum cardinalities to 0 while retaining the same maximums and broad semantic requirements text.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 base instances may omit fields that many R4 implementations treated as always present.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A min-cardinality decrease does not make R4 instances invalid in R6. It is still breaking for consumers and generated code that relied on non-null fields, and it creates a major R6-to-R4 problem because valid R6 instances can omit data required by R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Omitted insurer, provider, insurance, or product/service codes can impair adjudication, reconciliation, and analytics even if base R6 permits them.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow incomplete, staged, non-claim, or partially adjudicated records at the base resource level.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: decreased minimum cardinalities preserve R4-valid instances in base R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing omitted insurer, provider, insurance, or product/service data plausibly supports partial, staged, or broader workflow records. This relaxation creates important runtime and reverse-conversion risk, but it does not invalidate R4 instances moving to R6, so the backward-compatible alternative question is not applicable under this calibration.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base alternative is assessed for preserving R4 instances because the R4-required fields remain allowed in R6. Keeping the R4 minima would improve old code assumptions and R6-to-R4 round-tripping, but it would block the apparent R6 goal of permitting omissions at the base level rather than providing a less-breaking way to preserve R4-valid payloads. R6 profiles can re-require these fields for exchanges that need R4-like guarantees.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is R6-to-R4 representability and updated nullability assumptions, not an old-valid/new-invalid base validation break.

evidence.detail: R4 min is 1 for insurance.
R6 min is 0 for insurance.
R4 requires provider and insurer.
R6 makes provider and insurer optional.
R4 requires productOrService on six line-level elements.
R6 changes those minimums to 0.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment illustrates omission of fields that R4 required; it is not a full conformance example for all R6 business expectations.

findings.narrativeMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break, but it is one of the more important runtime and conversion risks. Many R4 implementations can safely dereference insurer, provider, insurance, and line product/service codes after validation; R6 base validation no longer provides that guarantee.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: no direct break from this relaxation. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: an R6 EOB that omits any of these formerly required fields cannot be converted to a valid R4 base resource without fabricating data or using extensions outside the R4 base cardinality model.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update consumers to treat these fields as optional in R6. Add profile-level requirements if an exchange still needs R4-like guarantees. For R6-to-R4 transforms, reject or quarantine records missing required R4 fields unless authoritative values can be derived.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Relaxing cardinality is backward-compatible for old instances but not for old code contracts. If the goal was partial-data support, profiles or workflow-specific resources could have preserved base guarantees for existing EOB consumers.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 makes several formerly required billing fields optional, including insurance, insurer, provider, and product/service codes on line structures. This does not reject R4 instances, but it does break old non-null assumptions in validators, generated models, and consumers that move to R6 data. The base relaxation appears intentional to allow partial or staged records, and profiles can re-require these fields for exchanges that need R4-like guarantees.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `insurance` min 1, `insurer` min 1, `provider` min 1.
R6 StructureDefinition: those same paths have min 0.
R4/R6 StructureDefinitions checked: item/detail/subDetail and addItem/detail/subDetail `productOrService` minima decrease from 1 to 0.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; the billing centrality makes nullability important, but there is no forward instance validation break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: old R4-derived code may assume non-null insurer, provider, insurance, and product/service after validation; R6-to-R4 loss occurs when valid R6 instances omit R4-required content.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No clearly better base design. Keeping the R4 minima would preserve old non-null contracts but would block the apparent R6 goal because FHIR profiles cannot relax a stricter base minimum. R4-like profiles are the appropriate compatibility mechanism for constrained exchanges.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the prior report correctly distinguished this from a hard R4-to-R6 instance break while flagging high runtime and reverse-conversion risk.

findings.title: Multiple reference targets were widened, creating R6-to-R4 representability risks

oldState.summary: R4 allowed narrower reference targets: enterer Practitioner|PractitionerRole, facility Location, prescription MedicationRequest|VisionPrescription, originalPrescription MedicationRequest, related.claim Claim.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 target profiles constrained the resource types that could appear in these references.

newState.summary: R6 adds targets: enterer Patient|RelatedPerson, facility Organization, prescription DeviceRequest|ServiceRequest, originalPrescription DeviceRequest|ServiceRequest|VisionPrescription, related.claim ExplanationOfBenefit.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can point to a broader set of request, author, facility, and related-claim resources.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding targets does not invalidate R4 instances in R6. It does mean R6-valid references can point to resource types that R4 validators and generated type constraints reject. Runtime code that switches on a closed set of target resource types must be updated.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misinterpreting request, facility, or related-claim references can change claim provenance and authorization context.

justification.inferredGoal: Support broader real-world authors, facilities, prescriptions/orders, and related EOB references.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: target additions preserve R4-valid references in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting additional author, facility, prescription/order, and related-claim targets is a plausible model improvement and is additive for R4-to-R6 validation. Existing R4 target types remain valid, so there is no less-breaking base design needed to preserve R4 instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because this is a forward-compatible target widening, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable. Profiles can restrict R6 targets for ecosystems that require R4 round-tripping, and downgrade transforms can reject or extension-map unsupported targets, but those are constraints or migration mitigations rather than less-breaking R6 base-design alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is R6-to-R4 downgrade policy and closed-union runtime handling for new targets, not old-instance preservation.

evidence.detail: R4 enterer targets Practitioner and PractitionerRole.
R6 enterer additionally targets Patient and RelatedPerson.
R6 adds Organization, DeviceRequest, ServiceRequest, VisionPrescription, and ExplanationOfBenefit in the listed locations.

examples.examplesMd: Each reference shown uses an R6 target that is not allowed by the corresponding R4 element.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 broadens several reference domains. This is safe for old R4 data moving forward, but it is a common source of reverse-conversion failures and runtime bugs in clients that generated closed reference unions from the R4 model.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: none from target additions. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: any added target type violates the corresponding R4 targetProfile restriction. Runtime: client code that assumes, for example, facility is always Location or related.claim is always Claim must be updated.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6 consumers, extend type handling and tests for each newly allowed target. For R6-to-R4, reject unsupported targets, map through extensions, or transform to a related allowed resource only when there is a documented business equivalence.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because this is additive in the forward direction, there is no clearly better R6 design for compatibility except retaining R4-restrictive profiles for ecosystems that need round-trip support.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The listed reference changes are target widenings: R4-allowed targets remain allowed and R6 adds Patient/RelatedPerson enterers, Organization facilities, more request types, and related ExplanationOfBenefit references. R6-to-R4 gateways and closed-union client code need policy for new target types, but this is not a base R4-to-R6 compatibility problem for existing EOB instances.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `enterer`, `facility`, `prescription`, `originalPrescription`, and `related.claim` have narrower targetProfile lists.

R6 StructureDefinition: the same paths retain the R4 target types and add Patient, RelatedPerson, Organization, DeviceRequest, ServiceRequest, VisionPrescription, or ExplanationOfBenefit as applicable.
Cardinalities and element paths remain present for the reviewed references.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; additive target widening is compatible with old data regardless of maturity.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: new R6 reference targets are not legal R4 targets, but R4 references are preserved in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable for R4-to-R6 compatibility. Restricting the target list would improve round-trip constraints but would remove R6 expressiveness; R4-compatible profiles can constrain target types where needed.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree: the prior report correctly notes reverse-conversion and runtime awareness, but its Medium overall impact overstates a forward-compatible target widening under the fresh-review rubric.

findings.title: supportingInfo.value[x] expanded from five choices to a broad DataType-like choice set

oldState.summary: R4 allowed boolean, string, Quantity, Attachment, or Reference(Resource).
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 supportingInfo values were constrained to a small set of common supporting-data representations.

newState.summary: R6 retains the R4 choices and adds many primitive, complex, metadata, and special-purpose datatypes including CodeableConcept, CodeableReference, Money, Period, Range, Ratio, Timing, Dosage, Meta, and others.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 choice domain is much closer to a general-purpose any-datatype slot.

facts.note: R6 snapshot lists Reference without a targetProfile.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using the old five choices remain structurally valid in R6. New R6 choices are not representable in the R4 element without converting them to string/Attachment/Reference/Quantity or using extensions, which may lose type semantics.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Supporting information can include adjudication evidence; lossy conversion can affect auditability or downstream rules.

justification.inferredGoal: Permit arbitrary supporting-data datatypes without forcing Attachment, string, Quantity, or Reference wrappers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R6 retains the R4 `value[x]` choices and only widens the allowed choice set.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A broader supporting-info value choice set reasonably improves expressiveness and does not remove the R4 boolean, string, Quantity, Attachment, or Reference choices. The compatibility concern is reverse conversion and parser coverage for new R6 suffixes, not R4-to-R6 instance preservation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 validity because old choices remain valid. Restricting R6 to the R4 choice set would preserve more R6-to-R4 round-trip behavior but would defeat the expressiveness goal. Profiles are the appropriate way to require R4-compatible supporting-info values in constrained exchanges.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is handling and downgrading new R6 datatypes; R4-compatible profiles can constrain the choice set when needed.

evidence.detail: R4 allowed boolean, string, Quantity, Attachment, and Reference(Resource).
R6 adds a broad set of primitive and complex datatypes while retaining the R4 choices.

examples.examplesMd: `valueMoney` is valid under the R6 choice set but has no direct R4 choice suffix.

findings.narrativeMd: `supportingInfo.value[x]` becomes far more permissive. This is useful for R6 authors but requires defensive parsing and explicit downgrade rules for any cross-version bridge.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: no direct break for the old choices. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: most new choice suffixes, such as `valueMoney`, `valueCodeableConcept`, `valuePeriod`, or `valueTiming`, cannot validate in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update R6 parsers and serializers to support the full choice list or constrain it with profiles. For downgrade, define datatype-specific conversions and preserve original R6 typed values with extensions when no lossless R4 representation exists.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This is a forward-compatible widening, so the compatibility concern is reverse conversion rather than old data. Profiles are the appropriate backward-compatible control point.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `supportingInfo.value[x]` keeps the R4 choices and adds many more datatypes. Existing R4 boolean, string, Quantity, Attachment, and Reference values remain structurally valid in R6. New R6 suffixes such as Money, Period, CodeableConcept, or Timing need R6 parser support and cannot always be sent back to R4, but that is normal additive evolution rather than a design problem for preserving old instances.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `supportingInfo.value[x]` allows boolean, string, Quantity, Attachment, and Reference(Resource).
R6 StructureDefinition: those choices are retained.
R6 StructureDefinition: many additional primitive and complex datatypes are added, including CodeableConcept, CodeableReference, Money, Period, Range, Ratio, Timing, Dosage, and Meta.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; it does not turn optional additive expressiveness into an R4-to-R6 break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6-only choice suffixes have no native R4 slot, but old R4 choice suffixes remain allowed.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable for forward compatibility. Omitting the added datatypes would preserve more reverse compatibility but would defeat the R6 expressiveness goal; profiles can restrict this choice set for R4-round-trippable exchanges.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree: the prior report correctly identifies reverse-conversion risk, but the fresh review treats retained old choices plus optional widening as No problem for R4-to-R6 compatibility.

findings.title: processNote.language binding strengthened from preferred common languages to required all-languages

oldState.summary: R4 processNote.language was CodeableConcept 0..1 with preferred binding to ValueSet/languages and maxValueSet all-languages.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 validators could warn but not fail solely because the language coding was outside the preferred common language value set.

newState.summary: R6 processNote.language is still CodeableConcept 0..1 but has required binding to ValueSet/all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4 with ValueSet/languages as a starter binding.

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires the CodeableConcept to include an IETF BCP-47 language code from all-languages.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a terminology validation strengthening. R4 instances with local or non-BCP47 language codings could be valid with at most a preferred-binding warning; R6 required binding can make them invalid. Confidence is medium because exact validator behavior depends on terminology expansion and CodeableConcept binding interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Require process-note language codings to use IETF BCP-47 language tags.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep base language binding non-required while using all-languages as preferred guidance and enforcing BCP-47 in profiles or warnings.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Requiring standard BCP-47 language tags is a reasonable interoperability goal, and the practical break is likely limited because common language codings should conform. A softer base binding would be less disruptive but would not deliver the same uniform validation guarantee.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept the base binding preferred or extensible, pointed implementers to `all-languages`, and required BCP-47 in profiles, best-practice invariants, or warning-level QA. That would preserve R4 instances with local-only language codings, but it is only a partial alternative because it relies on profile or tooling enforcement rather than making every base R6 `processNote.language` conform to the standard value set.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids hard failures for local R4 codings, but weakens uniform base validation of language tags.

evidence.detail: R4 binding strength is preferred to ValueSet/languages.
R6 binding strength is required to ValueSet/all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4.
R6 all-languages includes system urn:ietf:bcp:47.

examples.examplesMd: The invalidity of a local code depends on terminology validation; the example illustrates the strengthened required binding mechanism.

findings.narrativeMd: `processNote.language` keeps the same element shape but strengthens terminology conformance from preferred to required. This can turn a previously tolerated local language coding into a validation error.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: possible for CodeableConcepts without any coding in the required all-languages value set. R6-to-R4 is low risk because R4 had a preferred common-languages binding and a maxValueSet all-languages hint rather than a stricter incompatible domain.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Normalize note language codings to BCP-47 (`urn:ietf:bcp:47`) before R6 validation. Retain local language codes as additional codings only if a standard coding is also present. Include terminology-validation tests for missing, standard, and local-only language codings.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The stricter binding is interoperable but could have been phased in through profiles or warnings. Because the element is optional and common codes are likely standard, the practical risk is moderate rather than high.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A terminology server expansion would improve confidence about edge-case language tags and validator behavior.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `processNote.language` keeps the same optional CodeableConcept shape but strengthens the binding from preferred common languages to required all-languages. Local-only language codings that passed R4 structural validation can fail R6 terminology validation. The stricter BCP-47 language requirement is a reasonable interoperability goal, and the practical break is limited because the element is optional and standard language tags are broadly expected.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `processNote.language` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept` with preferred `ValueSet/languages` binding and a maxValueSet hint to all-languages.
R6 StructureDefinition: `processNote.language` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept` with required `ValueSet/all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4` binding.
R6 `ValueSet-all-languages` compose includes system `urn:ietf:bcp:47`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; the optional, terminology-only nature softens the concern, while business presentation of process notes keeps it from being dismissed entirely.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with local-only or text-only note language concepts may fail required-binding validation in R6, depending on terminology-validator behavior.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could keep the binding preferred or extensible and enforce BCP-47 in profiles or warnings, preserving more local R4 codings. That would be gentler but would not provide the same base-level assurance of interoperable language tags.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the prior report's potential hard break, medium impact, and partial less-breaking alternative are consistent with this fresh assessment.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The resource is present in both packages with the same canonical URL, id, type, kind, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract=false. Status changed from draft to active, recorded as a notable non-breaking change.
No local non-inherited constraints beyond base `ele-1`-style constraints were found in either snapshot.
No local isModifier flag changes were detected after excluding inherited base elements.
No material local isSummary flag changes were detected; undefined R4 mustSupport versus explicit false in R6 was not treated as a material change.
No local fixed, pattern, or defaultValue changes were detected in the compared elements.
No local slicing changes were detected for ExplanationOfBenefit elements in the base StructureDefinitions.

Required bindings for `status` and `use` point to R6-versioned value sets but packaged CodeSystems retain the same codes. `outcome` changes from remittance-outcome to claim-outcome; the packaged code list remains queued, complete, error, partial. Full terminology expansion was not performed.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The canonical identity and resource kind are unchanged. Status maturity can affect governance expectations but does not by itself invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat R6 ballot active status as stronger maturity than R4 draft, but still account for ballot-build instability.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds many optional local elements for events, encounters, decisions, trace numbers, taxes, patient-paid amounts, and review outcomes
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Most added elements have min=0, so existing R4 instances are not invalid merely because they lack them.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 systems can produce information that R4 has no base slot for, especially `event`, `encounter`, `decision`, `traceNumber`, `patientPaid`, `tax`, and nested `reviewOutcome` data. Downgrade paths need extensions or documented loss.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Several example bindings strengthened to preferred
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Preferred bindings are conformance guidance rather than hard validation requirements. They should not make otherwise valid instances fail base validation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Elements affected include careTeam.role, diagnosis.type, diagnosis.onAdmission, fundsReserve, item.adjudication.category, payment.adjustmentReason, payment.type, priority, procedure.type, and supportingInfo.category. Validators and QA tooling may emit stronger terminology warnings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: outcome required binding changed from remittance-outcome to claim-outcome with the same packaged code values
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The `outcome` element remains code 1..1 with required binding, and the packaged R4 remittance-outcome and R6 claim-outcome code systems both include queued, complete, error, and partial for the bound value sets relevant to this comparison.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated enum names, terminology canonical URLs, and analytics that key on the old ValueSet or CodeSystem URL should be reviewed even though instance code literals are preserved.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional statusReason
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element is optional (`0..1 string`), so R4 instances remain valid without it.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 producers may communicate reasons for status transitions that cannot be represented directly in R4 base ExplanationOfBenefit.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited DomainResource/Resource/Element changes were explicitly excluded from local findings and should be handled by the base artifact reports if material.

followUpDependencies.nameOrUrl: ExplanationOfBenefit-related ValueSets, especially all-languages, claim-outcome, note-type, and preferred claim/adjudication bindings
followUpDependencies.reasonMd: A terminology server expansion would confirm edge-case code validity and the exact impact of binding-strength changes.
Official ConceptMaps or StructureMaps would reduce ambiguity for patient-to-subject, packageCode-to-diagnosisRelatedGroup, careTeam qualification/specialty, and adjudication value/quantity mappings.
Profiles may re-require fields that R6 makes optional or restrict widened choice/reference domains, changing practical migration risk.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis did not use an official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot change notes, or JIRA rationale. Justification assessments are inferred from the computable artifacts.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review official HL7 change proposals, ballot reconciliation notes, or published R4/R5/R6 diff pages for ExplanationOfBenefit.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparison used packaged compose definitions and local CodeSystem concepts, not live expansions or validator behavior.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansions and validation examples against an R6-capable terminology server.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Expected prevalence is based on artifact semantics, not on a corpus of real-world R4 ExplanationOfBenefit instances.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Profile representative production or test EOB data for use of removed, reshaped, and newly optional elements.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Narrative specification pages were not inspected, so subtle prose-only semantics may be missed.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Compare the published R4 and R6 ExplanationOfBenefit narrative pages and examples.
